title: 7.2: A 2.2pJ/b 212.5Gb/s PAM-4 Transceiver with >46dB Reach in 5nm FinFET
problem: 100G/lane Ethernet is transitioning to 200G/lane (224Gb/s) to enable 1.6Tb/s infrastructure, requiring power-efficient, long-reach SerDes transceivers that handle signal integrity challenges from cables, connectors, and packages.
motivation: AI data centers demand higher bandwidth (200G/lane) to reduce network bottlenecks; achieving this at power and area efficiency is critical for infrastructure scaling.
method: The chip uses four-level signal encoding (PAM-4) to transmit data at 212.5 billion bits per second while compensating for signal degradation from cables and connectors. Built in 5-nanometer transistor technology, it includes specialized analog electronics that restore weakened signals, handling over 46 decibels of loss. This signal restoration happens efficiently, consuming only 2.2 picojoules of energy per bit transmitted.
key_novelty: This transceiver achieves long-reach performance (>46dB loss compensation) and low power consumption (2.2pJ/b) at 212.5Gb/s simultaneously, making dense 200-gigabit-per-lane data center interconnects practical.
contributions: 224Gb/s PAM-4 SerDes transceiver implementation in 5nm FinFET
Long-reach capability with >46dB channel loss compensation
Robust signal integrity handling for cables, connectors, and packages
limitations: Detailed analog/digital power breakdown, jitter performance, and latency specifications not provided; comparison with other 200G/lane solutions not quantified.
primary_theme: Efficient high-reach PAM-4 SerDes for 200G Ethernet
